data.title: Realty executives flag policy gaps, regulatory hurdles in Delhi's MPD-2047
data.description:
Delays in framing detailed policies, regulatory uncertainty and the involvement of multiple government agencies were among the key challenges that needed to be addressed for the implementation of Delhi's Master Plan 2047 (MPD-2047), top real estate executives said on Thursday at an Assocham event.
 
The MPD-2047, notified by the Union government in August, estimates that Delhi will need around 4 million additional housing units by 2047, when its population is projected to reach 32 million. The plan envisages meeting this demand through redevelopment, densification, transit-oriented development and planned urban expansion, supported by adequate infrastructure.
 
While describing the plan as forward-looking, developers said the supporting rules and regulations were yet to be formulated, which could delay the planning and execution of potential projects.
  
“Three or four months after notification, how many developers have filed applications for approvals? That is the proof of the pudding. It is a good plan, but a plan cannot execute itself,” said Gaurav Jain, vice-president of Naredco and managing director of Samyak Properties and Infra.
 
Jain said that while multiple agencies were involved, they would have to undertake an interactive approach to improve the implementation of the system, starting with approvals. “The question is how we execute these policies. The DDA and other agencies responsible for implementation need to be part of this conversation,” he said.
 
Vineet Kanwar, director and chief executive of DLF, said the Centre, the state government and the municipal corporation had separate responsibilities, complicating the process for developers.
 
“The central government controls some land, the state government handles other matters, and the municipal corporation has its own responsibilities. With so many agencies, it becomes difficult for developers to navigate the system,” he said.
 
Ankur Jalan, chief executive officer of Golden Growth Fund, a Sebi-registered Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), said the involvement of multiple agencies created uncertainty for investors. “Even if you own a parcel of land, you may not be able to develop it because you do not know how to obtain the required licence. Such uncertainty deters investors,” he said.
 
Sanjeev Ailawadi, head - legal at Max Estates, said the Centre, state and municipal authorities, along with other government agencies, often had overlapping roles and regulations, which needed simplification.

data.title: US Democrats plan 10-yr expiry for deportation orders, green card pathways
data.description:
US House Democrats will introduce legislation on Thursday that would provide relief to certain immigrants facing final orders of removal but with no criminal convictions, while creating a pathway for them to obtain lawful permanent residency, ABC News reported on Wednesday.
 
The proposed legislation, titled the Protect Our Neighbors Act, will be introduced by California Democratic Representative Lateefah Simon, according to the report.
 
Under the proposal, final orders of removal would expire 10 years after they were issued for individuals who have remained continuously in the US and have not been convicted of a crime. Currently, such orders have no expiration date.
  
The proposal has drawn criticism from former New York City Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) field director Scott Mechkowski, who confirmed the development in a post on X.
 
"Your deportation order now comes with an expiration date. That's the Bill House Democrats are introducing tomorrow. They're calling it the Protect Our Neighbors Act," he wrote.
 
Condemning the proposal, Mechkowski said, "Nobody should be rewarded with legal status for ignoring and evading our laws."
 
He outlined how the proposed provision would work.
 
"Here's how it works. A judge orders you removed. You lose your appeals. You don't leave. Stay ten years without a criminal conviction and the order goes away. Then they hand you a path to a green card," he wrote.
 
He argued that the legislation would reward individuals who failed to comply with deportation orders, while those who left the country as directed would not receive similar benefits.
 
"Think about that. The person who obeyed the judge and went home gets nothing. The one who ignored the order gets rewarded," he said.
 
Mechkowski also questioned the provision, arguing that the legislation could undermine the authority of immigration courts.
 
"These people already had their due process. A judge heard the case. It's over. This Bill says a court order means nothing if you outlast it," he wrote.
 
He further argued that delays caused by sanctuary policies could allow individuals to remain in the US long enough for their removal orders to expire. 
ALSO READ: US court strikes down Trump's plan to cap foreign students' visa stays
 
What happens to final deportation orders under the proposed Bill?
 
A final order of removal is issued by an immigration judge or immigration authorities and requires a non-US citizen to leave the country. The order becomes final after administrative appeals have been exhausted or the deadline for filing an appeal has passed.
 
Although a final removal order gives ICE the legal authority to deport an individual, it does not mean deportation takes place immediately or automatically. Removal proceedings can be delayed or suspended because of deferred action, a stay of removal, ongoing litigation or other circumstances.
 
Under the proposed legislation, an immigration judge could renew an expired final order of removal if the government establishes, through "clear and convincing evidence", that there was a substantial reason for the delay in carrying out the order.
 
The reason would have to be unrelated to administrative or funding delays. The judge would also have to determine that renewing the order was in the public interest based on new evidence, according to ABC report.
 
While Mechkowski criticised the legislation, immigration expert Andrea Flores welcomed the proposal.
 
"Glad to see the Protect Our Neighbors Act, which would create an earned path to legal residency for immigrants who may be left out of the American Dream and Promise Act," she wrote on X.
 
The legislation is also co-sponsored by California Democratic Representatives John Garamendi, Zoe Lofgren and Juan Vargas.
 
Former acting ICE Director Todd Lyons told lawmakers in February that approximately 1.6 million people in the US had final orders of deportation.
 
US deportations of Indian nationals
 
The proposed legislation comes amid expanded immigration enforcement under US President Donald Trump's second administration. The Department of Homeland Security and ICE have stepped up action against individuals with final orders of removal, including deportations to third countries.
 
Even immigrants who have regularly attended mandatory immigration check-ins have faced renewed risks of detention and deportation.
 
The development also follows Trump's remarks to CBS News' 60 Minutes, in which he said he would "love to do something on immigration" with Democrats, who are set to take control of both chambers of Congress in January following their victories in the midterm elections.
 
According to India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), the US deported 4,840 Indian nationals between January 2025 and July 2026. More than 6,000 Indians were deported during Trump's first presidential term, between 2017 and 2021.

data.title: Tata Sons board reviews Air India performance amid mounting losses
data.description:
Tata Sons board members, including Chairman N Chandrasekaran and Noel Tata, on Thursday reviewed the performance of loss-making Air India, according to sources.
 
Chandrasekaran, Noel Tata, and other board members Harish Manwani, Anita Marangoly George and Saurabh Agrawal visited the airline's headquarters and its training academy in Gurugram, they added.
 
They also visited the airline's Operations Control Centre (OCC).
 
Another board member, Venu Srinivas, was not present.
 
Air India MD and CEO Tewolde Gebremariam made a presentation on the airline's performance and plans to the board members, sources said.
 
The airline is co-owned by Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines.
 
The review by Tata Sons board members also comes a day before Air India's board meeting on Friday.
 
 
Integrating key operations of Air India and Air India Express, and plans for cost rationalisation, are likely to be discussed at the carrier's board meeting, sources said.
 
Surging fuel prices, Pakistan airspace restrictions disrupting long-haul flight operations, and other headwinds widened Air India's loss to more than ₹22,000 crore in FY26.
 
The airline, acquired by the Tatas from the government in January 2022, is in the midst of an ambitious transformation plan that has also faced hurdles, including supply chain woes hitting fleet upgradation and delaying aircraft deliveries.
 
On October 1, Ethiopian Airlines Group veteran Gebremariam took over the reins of Air India. He is the second foreigner to helm the carrier after Campbell Wilson, who stepped down earlier this year.
 
Gebremariam is focused on ways to reduce expenses and has urged Air India staff to embed a mindset of frugality and accountability in all their work. The airline has also set up a multi-disciplinary team to identify cost-saving opportunities.
 
On November 3, Gebremariam said Air India will rebalance its network, work to regain overseas market share, reduce costs and order more wide-body planes.
 
"In fact, more growth may come from the full-service (operations) wide-body (operations) because the opportunity there is much bigger.
 
"... on the LCC (Low Cost Carrier) side also, on Air India Express, there is growth. We want to position these brands to the customers of all segments in the market," he had said.
 
Meanwhile, Noel Tata has opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons Chairman on a slew of concerns, including the crucial question of its listing.
 
The financial performance of some of the bets, like the digital foray, Air India and the electronics business taken by Chandrasekaran, is also among Noel Tata's concerns.
 
On November 11, Singapore Airlines (SIA) said Air India has made tangible progress in its multi-year transformation, including enhancements to customer experience and operational performance.
 
"SIA and its partner, Tata Sons, recognise that a transformation of this scale will take time.
 
"Both partners continue to work closely to support Air India's journey towards profitable growth, including strengthening structural cost efficiencies, unlocking greater synergies between Air India and Air India Express, sharpening its commercial strategy to navigate current external challenges and elevating its customer proposition," SIA had said.

data.title: Sebi mulls Capacity Building Network to strengthen independent directors
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is exploring the creation of a Capacity Building Network (CBN) for independent directors to strengthen boardroom oversight and equip them to deal with emerging challenges such as cybersecurity, data governance and artificial intelligence (AI), Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Thursday.
 
Sebi and the National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM), along with industry associations, professional institutes, academic and technology institutions, and industry professionals, have initiated preliminary consultations to develop the proposed network, Pandey said at the Corporate Governance Summit.
 
The network is envisaged as a platform for peer learning, discussions on boardroom challenges, development of case studies and sharing of good governance practices.
 
 
“Ultimately, the strength of a board lies not merely in the diversity of expertise around the table, but also in its collective ability to learn, question and exercise sound judgement,” he stated.
 
Pandey said board members were increasingly expected to understand complex financial structures, regulatory developments and emerging technology-related risks, making one-time induction programmes and occasional training inadequate.
 
“Regulation will always have its limits. It cannot anticipate every business decision or prescribe the right response to every ethical dilemma. That responsibility must rest with corporate leadership and the gatekeepers of governance,” said Pandey.
 
He also outlined several regulatory initiatives aimed at strengthening corporate governance while improving ease of doing business.
 
On monitoring the utilisation of funds raised from investors, Sebi has recently issued a consultation paper proposing changes to the framework. These include strengthening the role of monitoring agencies, allowing them to submit reports directly to stock exchanges and extending monitoring requirements to issuances irrespective of their size, excluding offers for sale.
 
The regulator has also proposed changes to the framework governing action by stock exchanges against listed companies for regulatory non-compliance. The proposal seeks to avoid duplication of monetary penalties for companies listed on multiple exchanges, with a fine to be levied by only one exchange.
 
On sustainability disclosures, Pandey said Sebi's Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting framework covered the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation. Value-chain disclosures are required only for partners accounting for at least 2 per cent of an entity's total purchases and sales by value.
 
He said regulation alone could not ensure good governance, emphasising the need for independent judgement and accountability among boards, auditors and other gatekeepers.

data.title: REITs distribute ₹3,234 crore to over 5.25 lakh unitholders in Q2 FY27
data.description:
India's six publicly listed real estate investment trusts (REITs) collectively distributed over ₹3,234 crore to more than 5.25 lakh unitholders during the second quarter (Q2) of FY27, supported by strong demand for office space from global capability centres (GCCs) and front-office enterprises, the Indian REITs Association said in a statement on Thursday.
 
Commenting on the numbers, Shirish Godbole, chief executive officer of Knowledge Realty Trust and chairperson of the Indian REITs Association, said, “The distribution of Rs 3,234 crore during the quarter reflects the strength of India's REIT sector and its underlying assets. India is witnessing strong office demand, driven by both Global Capability Centres (GCCs) and front-office enterprises, creating a favourable environment for the sector.”
  
He pointed out that the investor base in REITs had crossed 5 lakh unitholders and continued to grow every quarter, reflecting increasing confidence in the sector.
 
As of Q2 FY27, the Indian REIT sector had total gross assets under management (AUM) of over ₹3.30 lakh crore. Its combined market capitalisation stood at over ₹2.09 lakh crore as of November 17, 2026, according to data mentioned in the statement.
 
Together, the six REITs manage more than 215 million square feet of Grade A office and retail space across India, the statement said.
 
Since their inception in 2014, they have cumulatively distributed over ₹38,000 crore to unitholders, highlighting the growing role of REITs in India's capital markets, it added.
 
The number of REIT unitholders has shown steady growth over the past three years, rising from around 2.55 lakh in Q2 FY25 to over 3.30 lakh in Q2 FY26 and crossing 5.25 lakh in the same quarter this year.
 
The six listed REITs in India are Brookfield India Real Estate Trust, Embassy Office Parks REIT, Mindspace Business Parks REIT, Nexus Select Trust, Knowledge Realty Trust and Bagmane Prime Office REIT.
 
According to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), REITs are mandated to distribute at least 90 per cent of their net distributable cash flows (NDCF). NDCF is the standard financial metric defined by Sebi to calculate the actual surplus cash available for payout to REIT investors.
 
REIT distributions are returns that can be in the form of dividends, interest, amortisation of debt received from special purpose vehicles, other income or a combination of these.

data.title: Manufacturing's share of GDP should rise to 25% by 2047: EAC-PM chairman
data.description:
India should raise the share of manufacturing in its gross domestic product (GDP) to 25 per cent by 2047 from the current 16-17 per cent to achieve its ambition of becoming a developed economy, S Mahendra Dev, chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM), said on Thursday.
 
“The share of manufacturing in GDP should rise from the present 16 to 17 per cent to 25 per cent by 2047. The transformation of the manufacturing sector is important for our goals at the time of the 100th year of India's independence,” Dev said in his address at the CII Financing Summit 2026.
 
 
He said India would need to sustain high economic growth over the next two decades to reach developed-country status. Dev said the country would need average real GDP growth of around 8 per cent annually over the next 21 years to achieve high-income status by 2047. He added that India had the potential to grow at 8-9 per cent, but sustaining this would require an expansion in productive capacity and improvements in productivity.
 
On the investment front, Dev said an investment rate of around 34-35 per cent of GDP would be important to sustain growth over the next two decades. Gross fixed capital formation stood at 31.9 per cent of GDP in 2025-26. He emphasised the need for greater private sector participation, saying public investment in infrastructure could encourage private investment by improving connectivity and reducing production and transportation costs. However, public investment alone would not be sufficient to meet the country's requirements.
 
Domestic savings would remain the principal source of financing India's investment requirements, Dev said. According to revised national accounts data, gross savings stood at 34.9 per cent of GDP in 2024-25, with the household sector accounting for around 62 per cent of the total. “Since households account for nearly two-thirds of India's domestic savings, the way these savings are used has an important bearing on how investment elsewhere in the economy is financed,” he said.
 
He said foreign capital could supplement domestic savings, but the country's own savings would remain the foundation for sustaining investment over the long term.
 
Dev also called for diversifying sources of long-term finance, saying banks alone could not meet the financing requirements of India's development ambitions. “Different investments require different kinds of finance. These requirements cannot all be met through conventional bank lending,” he said, highlighting the role of insurance and pension funds, corporate bond markets and equity markets in financing long-term investments.
 
India's corporate bond market, however, remains concentrated among highly rated issuers, with around 85-90 per cent of issuances in the highest-rated securities, Dev said. Mid-sized companies and lower-rated borrowers continue to have limited access to the market.
 
On exports, he said India's combined merchandise and services exports had reached approximately $863 billion in 2025-26, and the country was expected to cross $1 trillion in exports this year. Improving competitiveness, diversifying export markets and strengthening participation in global value chains would be crucial amid rising protectionism and geopolitical uncertainty.
 
Dev also stressed the importance of structural transformation in agriculture, manufacturing and services, alongside greater use of technology and digital public infrastructure. He called for improving agricultural productivity through diversification, post-harvest activities and agro-processing, while strengthening farmer producer organisations.
 
He said states would have to play a crucial role in achieving the 2047 vision, with each state setting its own development targets. Less-developed states such as Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh would have a greater role in India's future economic and social development.
 
“Political stability, macroeconomic stability and a large domestic economy” were the three factors underpinning India's resilience, Dev said, adding that global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty remained a key concern.

data.title: NTA UGC NET December 2026 schedule out, check subject-wise exam dates
data.description:
The National Testing Agency (NTA) has released the subject-wise exam schedule for the University Grants Commission National Eligibility Test (UGC NET) December 2026 session. As per the official notice, the exam will occur from December 14 to 18 and on December 21, 2026 in CBT mode. 
 
Candidates can check the complete subject-wise timetable on the official website, ugcnet.nta.nic.in. The exam will be held in two shifts each day: from 9 am to 12 noon, and the second shift from 3 pm to 6 pm.  

UGC NET December 2026 Important Dates

Online Registration Dates:- October 8 to October 31, 2026
 
Correction Window:- November 2 to November 4, 2026 
 
 
Exam City Intimation Slip:- 21 days before the exam 
 
Admit Card:- 3 to 10 days before the exam date
 
Exam Dates:- December 14 to December 18 and December 21, 2026.

How to download the UGC NET December 2026 exam schedule?

• Visit the official portal of the UGC NET NTA at ugcnet.nta.nic.in. 
 
• Locate the Public Notices section on the homepage, or open the NTA 2026 Public Notices Archive.
 
• Click on the link titled "Public Notice for Subject-wise schedule of UGC-NET December 2026 Examination-Reg." (or access the Direct NTA Schedule PDF).
 
• Open the PDF and locate Annexure-I. Match your Subject Code and Subject Name to verify your exact exam date and shift timing.
 
Save by downloading or printing the PDF timetable for future use. 
ALSO READ: CGBSE board exam dates 2027: Chhattisgarh Class 10, 12 datesheet released

UGC NET December 2026 city intimation slip and admit card

As per the NTA's public notice, the exam city intimation slip will be released on the official website 21 days before the respective examination date. On the other hand, the admit card will be issued 3 to 10 days before the exam date.

data.title: Moody's upgrades PNB's credit assessment on better asset quality, profits
data.description:
Moody's Ratings on Thursday affirmed state-run Punjab National Bank's ratings and upgraded the baseline credit assessment, citing improvements in capital, asset quality, and profitability.
 The outlooks on PNB's long-term deposit and issuer ratings are stable, in line with the stable outlook on India's sovereign rating. PNB's solvency and liquidity metrics are expected to be stable over the next 12-18 months, the US-based rating agency said.
 Moody's said it expects the bank's internal capital generation to support growth over the next 12-18 months, although the transition to the Expected Credit Loss (ECL) framework and revised investment valuation norms from fiscal 2027 will likely reduce capital.
 
 "The affirmation of PNB's Baa3 ratings and upgrade of BCA to Baa3 from Ba1 reflects the improvement in its capital, asset quality and profitability.
 "The bank's funding and liquidity profiles remain key credit strengths, underpinned by its status as a public-sector bank and extensive branch network," Moody's said.
 PNB's asset quality continues to improve. Its gross NPL ratio declined to 2.6 per cent in September 2026 from 3.5 per cent in September 2025.
 Moody's expects some deterioration in agriculture and MSME loans as irregular rainfall, El Nino conditions and inflation pressure borrowers' repayment capacity.
 These sectors are more vulnerable to shocks because agricultural borrowers have limited income buffers and MSMEs have less ability to pass on higher costs, the rating agency said.
 "However, we expect overall asset quality to remain stable over the next 12-18 months, supported by recoveries and write-offs outpacing new NPL formation," it added

data.title: New launches to keep Oberoi Realty's sales momentum elevated in FY27
data.description:
Mumbai-based realty major Oberoi Realty outperformed top listed peers in the September quarter on the pre-sales/bookings front. The company reported its highest-ever quarterly pre-sales of ₹9,150 crore in Q2FY27, which was seven times higher year-on-year (Y-o-Y) and nine times higher on a sequential basis. The gains were largely due to the launch of its Gurugram project, Three Sixty North, which received a strong response.
 
After the successful launch of the Gurugram project, the company is eyeing launches of projects/towers across Mumbai and Thane over the next two years. Brokerages are also positive about the steady annuity income from its commercial portfolio, which offers cash flow visibility. At the current price (₹1,802), the stock, which has gained about 14 per cent over the past six months, is trading at a discount to its FY27 net asset value.
 
Of the overall pre-sales in Q2, about 85 per cent was accounted for by Three Sixty North, Gurugram. In the Gurugram project, about 97 per cent of the launched area was booked at a realisation of ₹59,961 per square foot. The rest of the pre-sales were accounted for by its Mumbai projects, Elysian (Goregaon) and 360 West (Worli), at ₹350 crore and ₹280 crore, respectively. Other notable Mumbai project contributions include Sky City and Jardin, which notched up pre-sales of ₹120 crore to ₹180 crore.
 
Elara Securities points out that the realtor delivered a positive surprise on sustenance sales of ₹1,260 crore, which is 25 per cent above both the Street's and its own estimates. This, according to analysts led by Rahul Jain of the brokerage, creates upside risk to the full-year pre-sales estimate of ₹14,400 crore. The company ended the first half of FY27 with pre-sales of ₹10,200 crore. The expectation of higher bookings in FY27 is on account of the planned launches in H2FY27 (Mumbai and adjoining areas), including Peddar Road, one tower each in Pokhran and Kolshet, and uber-luxury villas at Alibaug.
 
The brokerage has a 'buy' rating on the stock with a target price of ₹2,800 and views Oberoi as a low-risk compounder led by prudent underwriting through cycles, with land costs at less than 5 per cent of gross development value. Further, it has a deep micro-market presence with 25 per cent, 14 per cent and 11 per cent volume market shares in Goregaon, Borivali and Mulund, respectively, during FY21-26 and has also evolved into a multi-regional player following the Gurugram launch. It trades at an attractive 20 per cent discount to its March 2027 estimated net asset value.
 
In the annuity business, rental income increased 18 per cent Y-o-Y and 2 per cent sequentially to ₹320 crore during the quarter. The commercial portfolio occupancy stood at 98 per cent during the quarter. The annuity segment's performance was led by Sky City Mall, which achieved 83 per cent occupancy compared to 82 per cent in Q1 and 53 per cent in Q2FY26. Revenues in the hospitality business grew by 2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹45.6 crore. PL Capital expects annuity income to remain steady at ₹1,300 crore to ₹1,400 crore by FY28, providing strong cash flow visibility. The brokerage has upgraded the stock to 'buy' from 'accumulate', with a target price of ₹2,100.
 
JM Financial Research expects the company to sustain an annual sales run rate of ₹10,000 crore to ₹12,000 crore, compared to ₹4,500 crore to ₹5,500 crore during FY23-26, aided by multiple launches. The annuity vertical, according to analysts led by Sumit Kumar of the brokerage, will also stabilise soon, resulting in strong cash flows that can comfortably support capex and business development. It has a 'buy' rating with a target price of ₹2,250.
